questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Order four hardware technologies in a conventional introductory account of computer generations.
questions.prompt: A museum display has mixed up four cards: microprocessor, vacuum tubes, integrated circuits and individual transistors. Put the cards in the usual order of the hardware milestones and explain what changed when individual transistors gave way to integrated circuits.
questions.answer: Vacuum tubes, individual transistors, integrated circuits, microprocessors. Integrated circuits put multiple electronic components together on one chip instead of building the logic entirely from separately packaged devices.
questions.explanation: These labels describe major developments. Actual machines could use a mixture of technologies during transitions.

markingGuide.description: Explains integration of multiple components onto a chip.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Explain a physical advantage of switching technology in early computers.
questions.prompt: A display shows two early computer assemblies that perform similar switching work. One uses rows of glass vacuum tubes. The other uses much smaller semiconductor transistors. Give two reasons why a designer might choose the transistor assembly for a machine that must fit in less space.
questions.answer: Smaller transistors can fit more switching components in a given space. Their lower power use can also reduce the heat that needs to be removed.
questions.explanation: Component size affects packing density, and power use affects cooling needs.

markingGuide.description: Connects smaller components to a concrete space advantage.
Connects lower power use to reduced cooling needs.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.subtopic: Distinguishing a processor chip from a logic chip
questions.learningObjective: Explain what distinguishes a microprocessor from an integrated circuit used for a smaller function.
questions.prompt: A display includes one chip that performs a single logic function and another chip that executes the instructions for an entire computer as its central processor. Both are integrated circuits. Which is a microprocessor in this example, and why?
questions.answer: The second chip is a microprocessor because it implements the central processor on one chip and executes instructions.
questions.explanation: Integrated circuit is the broader term. Computing instructions are the distinguishing function in this example.

markingGuide.description: Explains its role in executing instructions.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Identify the Nigerian body associated with professional computing registration.
questions.prompt: A pupil is preparing a careers display and needs an official source on registration of computing professionals in Nigeria. Which body should the pupil consult, and why is a job advertisement a weaker source?
questions.answer: Consult the Computer Professionals Registration Council of Nigeria, or CPN. It publishes information about professional registration and oversight. A job advertisement states an employer’s requirements for a vacancy.
questions.explanation: The council describes its own registration responsibilities. The advertisement has a different purpose.

markingGuide.description: Explains why the council is the relevant source for registration.

questions.subject: Digital Technologies
questions.learningObjective: Identify a Nigerian professional society and explain a reason to consult it.
questions.prompt: A teacher wants a Nigerian professional society to consult for a careers event that introduces pupils to computing practitioners and professional networking. Name a body that fits and explain the connection.
questions.answer: The Nigeria Computer Society fits because it brings together computing and IT professionals and stakeholders and supports professional cooperation.
questions.explanation: A professional society is a source of information about its community and activities.

markingGuide.description: Connects its professional community or cooperation to the careers event.
